reason: Verified in the source and by driving the page. render-b.js move() clamps only the floor (`if (current < 1) current = 1;`) and writes `item.style.top = current * px` with no ceiling and no post-move layout check. Driven at 1440x960, ?v=approach&state=owner-editing: one press of "Move a week earlier" puts the invitations at away=16, the same count as "Menu tasting at The Orchard", both at offsetTop 224 and both rects at top 467 — the two titles, the two date lines and the two SHOWN chips print on top of each other as unreadable overprint (screenshot captured). It is not confined to the exact same day either: four presses of -1 lands 19 against the menu's 16, a 3-day gap of 42px against a row that is 79px tall, so the invitation's rect (top 509) cuts 37px into the menu's (bottom 546) and the date lines still overprint. In the other direction there is no ceiling at all: twenty presses of +7 reach "in 149 days" at top 2086px inside a .b-measure whose inline height stays 1198px, an item placed 888px below the bottom of the measure and 70 days past a horizon that still reads 79, silently. The gate does not cover this: interaction-check.mjs runs its proportionality and collision assertions only on first paint of phone/desk/owner-flight/print, and its stepper block performs the very -7 press that causes the collision but asserts only that the item moved nearer, that nothing else moved, that the readouts agree and that scroll and focus survive. The collision is never re-measured after the gesture. This is the direction's own stated law (a pixel is a real unit of time, no two items ever touch) failing after a single press of the primary gesture, which is a genuine defect at the 9.5 bar and not something automation already proves.
sharpenedFix:
Correct in shape, wrong in three details, and it misses a fourth defect sitting in the same function.

1. Ceiling and floor: clamp move() to 1…F.toDay() as proposed, and set aria-disabled="true" on +1/+7 at the ceiling with a one-line reason. Keep the reason in the page's own grammar rather than a second one — the stepper readout already speaks in "in N days", so say "The day itself is in 79 days" there, not a new sentence in a new tense.

2. The stale date, which the finding names in its evidence but does not fix: move() rewrites .b-away and .b-stepRead only. After -7 the row prints "16" beside "SAT 8 AUG", and the .b-grab aria-label still announces "Saturday 8 August 2026, in 23 days". Recompute the ISO date from TODAY + count and rewrite .b-date and the .b-grab label in the same pass. A row that prints a count and a date that disagree is worse than a collision, because it is legible and wrong.

3. The 8px threshold is too small by an order of magnitude and would not catch the 3-day case measured above. Compare measured rects, not a constant: after every move, walk the sorted .b-item rects and flag any pair where rects[i].top < rects[i-1].bottom, the same predicate interaction-check.mjs already uses at first paint. Reuse it rather than inventing a second rule.

4. The merge as written can trade one collision for another. Two titles stacked inside one row makes that row taller than the ~79px the 14px/day scale was derived from, so a merged pair can then overprint the next item at the 7-day gap the scale was chosen to clear. Any merge must re-measure its own height against the following item and, if it no longer clears, refuse the move rather than render the overlap — and refusing must be stated ("That lands on the same day as Menu tasting") rather than absorbed silently, which is the same failure the ceiling has today.

Gate additions: put the assertions in the same block as the existing stepper test, and drive a sequence, not one press — after a run of presses that includes a same-day landing (-7) and a near landing (four x -1), assert no two .b-item rects overlap, no item's offsetTop exceeds .b-measure's offsetHeight, and no .b-away exceeds F.toDay().
